Every provider names these differently — Acefone calls a number a My Number, Ozonetel calls it a Virtual Number — but they are the same four things, so a new provider reuses this screen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Telephony Account — one per provider tenant. Its webhook token is what authenticates the provider; HMAC and an IP allowlist are optional and off until you turn them on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Numbers (DIDs) — one row per number the business gives you, and the grain it belongs to. A number that is not listed here is dropped. That is what keeps other businesses off a shared provider account out of this CRM. Type the number; pick the grain — it must match the grain on the leads, or a call attaches to nothing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Agents — only for agents whose provider email is not their CRM login. Staff whose email matches a CRM user resolve on their own and need no row. An unmapped agent never costs you the call; it only leaves the rep blank.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tel4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Capture Rules — inside Telephony Settings. Which calls become Call Logs, by direction and channel. Empty captures nothing; telephony is on once you add a rule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every delivery is logged either way. A call that is dropped or declined is recorded in Integration Request with the reason — fix the reason, replay the row, and the call lands.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "telsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Telephony Accounts", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Telephony Routing", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "User Mapping", "col": 3}}, {"id": "telsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Capture Rules", "col": 3}}, {"id": "voicehdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "AI Voice Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "voiceintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Three steps, in order. An AI voice call is placed by a workflow and never by hand — the account below carries the credentials, and the agent that does the talking is chosen on the workflow node itself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "voice1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. AI Voice Account — one per provider tenant. The API key, the base URL and the number calls are placed from are held here, and its webhook token is what authenticates the provider's callbacks. An account that is not enabled places nothing, so credentials can be entered and checked long before anything is dialled.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "voice2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Webhook URL — shown on the account form once a token is generated, and registered against the agent in the provider's own dashboard. How a call ended is reported back through it; until it is registered a workflow waits on an outcome that never arrives.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "voice3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. The AI Voice Call node — added to a workflow, where the account and the agent are picked and the person to call is referenced from the lead. What happens next is branched on there: answered, no answer, completed or failed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "voiceafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every callback is logged either way. A number carrying no country code is refused before any call is placed, and outbound calls are made only while automation sending is switched on — with it off, a workflow runs to the same point and dials nobody.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "voicesc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "AI Voice Accounts", "col": 4}}, {"id": "trhdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Transcription Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "trintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two steps, in order. A transcript is posted to the CRM by the service that produced it — nothing is fetched or polled — and it is stored against the call it belongs to, in the same shape every transcript takes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tr1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Transcription Account — one per service tenant. Its webhook token is what authenticates the service, and HMAC signing and an IP allowlist are optional and off until they are turned on. An account that is not enabled authenticates nothing, so credentials can be entered and checked long before any transcript is accepted.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tr2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Webhook URL — shown on the account form once a token is generated, and registered with the transcription service. Text arrives through it and is attached to the call; until it is registered, calls keep their audio and stay without a transcript.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "trafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every delivery is logged either way. A transcript posted for a call this CRM never placed is refused rather than invented, and a re-transcription REPLACES the text it corrects instead of stacking a second copy.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "trsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Transcription Accounts", "col": 4}}]
